feed.title: Apple Says Smartphones, Tablets Don’t Infringe 5G Tech Patents
feed.summary: Apple has filed a complaint against Hannibal IP LLC in a California federal court, alleging that the patent assertion company breached a contract by prematurely ending 5G technology licensing negotiations and subsequently suing Apple for patent infringement. Apple claims that Hannibal IP, affiliated with Longhorn IP LLC, engaged in negotiations since 2022 but then unexpectedly filed a lawsuit in a Texas federal court in August, asserting that Apple's smartphones and tablets infringe their patents. This legal action suggests a breakdown in what Apple perceived as ongoing and collaborative discussions between the two entities.

feed.title: Q3 PC units down 22.4% YoY
feed.summary: PC shipments in Q3 2026 declined by 22.4% year-over-year to 55.4 million units, primarily due to higher memory and storage costs leading to increased PC pricing. All top six worldwide PC vendors experienced declines, with Lenovo maintaining market leadership despite a 22.4% drop and Apple showing the lowest decline among them.

feed.title: Trump’s Russia Tariff Waiver Helps Apple, Eliminates Tariff Advantage for CF and CVR Partners
feed.summary: President Trump's waiver of sanctions and tariffs under the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act provides temporary relief for Apple and other companies manufacturing in China and India, preventing potential 100% tariffs on imported goods. This move also benefits diesel consumers by keeping Russian fuel flowing, but it eliminates a potential advantage for domestic fertilizer producers like CF Industries Holdings Inc. and CVR Partners LP, who might have benefited from increased protection. The waiver, however, is temporary, with a 60-day review period that could lead to a reversal of the decision in December.
